name: Ignore battery optimization
plain: Asks to be exempt from Doze and app standby.
meaning: Lets the app run in the background more freely at the cost of battery. The user confirms with a dialog.

android.prompt_ui: System dialog: Allow app to run in background
android.store_policy: Play: restricted; allowed only when core function breaks under Doze
android.note: Declared as a normal permission; the exemption needs user confirmation.

ios.note: iOS gives no such exemption; use Background Modes or push.

limits.headline: Can ask to keep running in the background on Android, only if you agree
limits.user_action: A system box asks if the app may run in the background and you tap Allow
can: Ask you to turn off battery limits for the app
Stay awake longer in the background once you allow it
Use less strict Doze and standby rules after you agree
cannot: Turn off battery limits without your yes
Get this exemption on iPhone, which has none
Use it forever if you later change your battery setting
limits.reach_label: Ongoing, but only after your OK
limits.differs: Android shows a system confirmation. iPhone has no such exemption; apps use background modes or push.

story.what_it_is: Asks to be excused from Android's rules that put idle apps to sleep.

marketing.name: Doze and App Standby
marketing.pitch: Google describes Doze and standby as ways to save battery by putting idle apps to sleep, with some exceptions.

story.for_you: You see a pop up asking Allow app to always run in the background. If you say yes, the app works more reliably but may cost more battery.
story.for_makers: Makers want reliable alerts and syncing for chats, health and tracking. Google limits who may ask, because it hurts battery life.

use_cases.example: A chat app asks to stay awake so messages are never late.
A medical sensor app asks for it so alerts are never missed.
A fitness tracker asks for it to record a full ride without gaps.
A home security app asks for it so door alerts are instant.
A game asks for it to keep a multiplayer match alive in the background.
A field work app asks for it to keep location checks running on a shift.
A VPN or file sync app asks for it so it does not disconnect.

risks: Apps may nag you to allow it
story.android_note: You confirm in a system dialog. It is a standard permission with a user check.
story.ios_note: iOS has no such exemption. Apps use background modes or push messages.
